title: Flavored Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems to Lower Smoking and Exposure to Tobacco Toxicants Among Cigarette Smokers Interested in Quitting, REFLECT Trial
official: Two-Arm Randomized Clinical Trial of Individuals Who Smoke Tobacco Cigarettes and Initiate ENDS Use With Fruit or Tobacco Flavors (Reducing Smoking With Flavored E-Cigarettes Trial; REFLECT)
summary: This clinical trial studies whether different flavored electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS) help lower smoking and exposure to tobacco toxicants among cigarette smokers interested in reducing their smoking. ENDS are battery-powered electronic devices designed to deliver a nicotine-containing liquid solution for inhalation. They do not burn tobacco. Previous research has shown that ENDS have the potential to lower exposure to potentially toxic substances compared to burned cigarettes as well as lower short-term adverse health outcomes. However, there are many different ENDS products with varying characteristics, including different flavors, and a need remains to understand more how flavors affect ENDS use, the potential reduction in cigarette use, and exposure to toxicants. This trial studies how two different flavors, fruit and tobacco, affect an individual's smoking behavior and ultimately whether flavored ENDS can help lower smoking and exposure to tobacco toxicants among cigarette smokers interested in reducing their smoking.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Be a regular cigarette smoker, defined as \>= 5 CPD for at least 12 months. Smoking status will be bio-verified via salivary cotinine (\>= 30 ng/mL) and exhaled breath carbon monoxide (CO) \> 10 parts per million (ppm) at the baseline visit
* A history of cigarette use for \>= 2 years
* Have at least a moderate interest in quitting smoking (defined as \>= 4 on a Likert-style 1-10 scale, where 10 represents the greatest interest)
* No regular daily ENDS use in the past 12 months
* Participant (or legal representative) must understand the investigational nature of this study and sign an Independent Ethics Committee/Institutional Review Board-approved written informed consent form prior to receiving any study-related procedure

Exclusion Criteria:

* Presence of clinically significant health issues or illnesses, including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), or cancer (as self-reported during phone pre-screening and confirmed at baseline visit screening)
* Patients at Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center, regardless of cancer diagnosis status
* Pregnant or nursing female participants (self-reported on telephone screener, self-reported and bio-verified with urinary pregnancy test at baseline visit)
* Use of nicotine products other than cigarettes within 7 days before the baseline visit (self-reported during phone pre-screening and confirmed at the baseline visit)
* Use of any other tobacco products, including cigarillos, cigars, little cigars, or oral nicotine pouches, more than 1 day per week within 30 days before the baseline visit (self-reported during phone pre-screening and confirmed at the baseline visit)
* Use of smoking cessation medications within 3 months before the baseline visit (self-reported during phone pre-screening and confirmed at the baseline visit)
